content.user_title: Edit Images with Flux Kontext Pro
content.value_statement: Precise image edits can drift when prompts are vague or the wrong model is chosen. This skill guides Flux Kontext Pro edits on RunComfy with focused prompts and routing advice.
actual_capabilities: Routes explicit Flux Kontext image-edit requests to the RunComfy model endpoint.
Documents required input fields: prompt, image, optional aspect_ratio, and seed.
Provides RunComfy CLI examples for local edits and seeded variants.
Compares Flux Kontext with Nano Banana Edit, GPT Image 2 edit, and Flux 2 Klein.
Supplies prompt patterns for preservation-led local image edits.
Explains RunComfy token storage, endpoint behavior, output downloads, and exit codes.
limitations: Supports one source image per request; multi-image edits need another model.
Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and network access.
Public model fields may change, so production workflows should check the model page.
Compound prompts can drift and may need sequential edit passes.

use_cases.title: Product Image Revision
use_cases.description: Update a label, color, or small object while preserving product shape, lighting, and framing.

use_cases.title: Portrait Micro-Edit
use_cases.description: Add or adjust one visible detail while preserving identity, pose, clothing, and composition.

use_cases.title: Model Selection Check
use_cases.description: Decide whether a request belongs in Flux Kontext or another RunComfy image model.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Local Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Flux Kontext Pro for this image. Keep the subject, pose, lighting, and framing unchanged. Add a red scarf around the subject.

prompt_templates.title: Preserve Brand Asset
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit this product image with Flux Kontext. Keep the bottle shape, table, lighting, and label placement unchanged. Replace only the label text with AURA.

prompt_templates.title: Refine With Seed
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Flux Kontext edit using a fixed seed. Keep the original identity and background unchanged, then change only the jacket color to navy.

prompt_templates.title: Choose The Right Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this image-edit request and decide whether Flux Kontext is the right model. If yes, write a preservation-led prompt for RunComfy.

output_examples.input: A portrait needs one added object while the person remains unchanged.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Flux Kontext, asks for one public image URL, and produces a concise preservation-led edit prompt.

output_examples.input: A product label needs a controlled text replacement.
output_examples.output: The skill emphasizes unchanged shape, lighting, and placement, then isolates the requested label text change.

output_examples.input: A request includes several source images and a complex scene change.
output_examples.output: The skill advises using a different model because Flux Kontext is designed for one source image and targeted edits.

best_practices: Start prompts with what must stay unchanged before naming the edit.
Use one clear source image and one targeted change per run.
Use a seed when comparing variants or repeating an edit.
anti_patterns: Do not combine many unrelated edits in one Flux Kontext prompt.
Do not use this skill for multi-image workflows.
Do not rely on it for text-heavy multilingual image editing.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides precise single-image edits with Flux Kontext Pro through the RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: Does it generate images from scratch?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for editing one existing source image.

faq.question: What inputs are required?
faq.answer: It needs one image URL and one clear edit prompt. Aspect ratio and seed are optional.

faq.question: When should I choose another model?
faq.answer: Choose another model for multi-image edits, image generation from scratch, or complex embedded text changes.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill expects the RunComfy CLI to be installed and authenticated.

faq.question: Can I use it in Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
